Notes

  • Why it's strong: the ring is the one element that exists physically (the Dock), on screen (status), and in the logo — one shape carrying the whole brand. It also solves the "RE REPAPER" duplication: the RE is the wordmark, the ring just frames it.
  • R1 vs R2: R1 keeps the two-tone wordmark and adds the ring — busier but unmistakable. R2 is calmer: white letters, one green ring — the green becomes the light, not the type. R2 is closer to the "glow is light, never ink" rule.
  • R3 (gap) reads as "on / loading / refresh" — that's a feature (the ring breathes) but also close to the power symbol; the gap angle matters.
  • R4 (orbit) is the most distinctive and the hardest to use: it needs lots of clear space, doesn't reduce well, and the crossing points must land between letters. Better as a hero/booth treatment than as the everyday lockup.
  • Standalone: ring + RE works as an icon down to 32 px; at 16 px only the ring survives — which is fine: the ring alone is the favicon.
  • Ring stroke = stem weight of the R (≈ 0.15 em). The ring sits so its centre is the optical centre of RE; the crossing on the right falls in the gap before P — in the final SVG the P gets a little extra space.

Notes for stage 2

  • Trace it, don't use the PNG. Cyan anti-aliasing fringes and speckles; branch joints have notches and double edges. Threshold → trace → straighten every edge; rebuild the five leaves as one pentagon repeated.
  • Small sizes: at 16 px the leaves merge. A reduced version (three leaves, thicker trunk) for favicon and app icon.
  • Brand rule: "no eco imagery" gets rewritten: the tree is ours, always faceted/geometric, never a soft illustrated leaf.
